_notes: The fighter design pass's target card (notes/fighter-design.md, ROADMAP Decisions step 4 'Changed 2026-11-12 late'): plane-sheet numbers each fighter is built to by tools/fit-planes.mjs. topSpeed and climbRate at low level (y 300), turnTime from 80% of top speed, slowTurnTime from 1.4 x stall, diveSpeed after a 60 degree dive losing 300, topSpeedHigh at y 1000. hp is set as it is. The tuner then fine-tunes within ±15% around these. Revised 2026-11-12 with the propeller physics (fast planes dive fast: both come from low drag) and history (the P-47 was not slow at sea level): P-47 top 150 and the best dive 240, La-5FN top 165 and dive 225, Spitfire top 158. La-5FN: climb 62 and dive 232 (fastest low needs low drag and strong pull; it climbed nearly as well as the Spitfire). La-5FN high 130: thin air keeps about 80% of low-level speed even at the lowest rated height, so weak high means losing the most going up. P-47 climb 40 and dive 245: the best dive needs the lowest drag, so less thrust and a weaker climb (history: about a third below the Spitfire).
